edits.content:
## Audit near-identical mathematical claims
- Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note any cutoff, the order of iterated limits, whether the claim uses a limit or limsup, and the stated norm. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
- When choices share a base existence or invariance claim, assess every added property as a separate obligation. Generic behavior or dimension intuition does not establish a claim about every fiber, nor does rational existence by itself imply regularity or a codimension bound.
- For competing displayed formulas, compare coefficients, index ranges, and phrases such as “only one” versus “at most one” independently. Use the definitions of the quantities to check which terms and indices the equation should involve.
